Candidate 0 best combines predictable staple supply, modest coordination demands, consistent allocation and an inspectable trial. Buffering imposes immediate-access costs; the other approaches depend more on local demand, arrival patterns or record quality.

Candidate 5 offers the strongest balance: recurring staple commitments, explicit correction of missed-delivery information, a bounded replacement attempt through existing donors, equal access and required tracking. Its donor-contact prerequisite and limits are stated clearly.
